threat: Malicious/compromised page script passes hostile input (wrong types, circular refs, getter/proxy traps, prototype-pollution keys, unicode/control chars, oversized attribute counts, reserved fields, secret-shaped values) to the 6 public exports
attackSurface: packages/browser-observability public API (initializeObservability, setTrackingConsent, recordAction, recordError, getObservabilityStatus, shutdownObservability)
expectedBehavior: Never throws to the host; unsafe payloads are dropped/redacted; raw payload never reaches status/log/storage; public API stays exactly 6 exports

threat: Attacker-shaped object key (__proto__/constructor/prototype, e.g. from JSON.parse) reshapes the sanitized attributes/context object's prototype instead of being stored as a data property
attackSurface: packages/browser-observability/src/sanitization/sanitizers/attributes.js (feeds both recordAction attributes and recordError context)
expectedBehavior: Reserved object-shaped keys are rejected as ATTRIBUTE_KEY_FORBIDDEN like any other forbidden key; the sanitized object's prototype is always Object.prototype

threat: A single recordAction()/recordError() call with one large string attribute/message freezes the host page's JS main thread via super-linear regex-based PII/secret detection
expectedBehavior: Sanitization completes in bounded time regardless of input length; no realistic secret pattern goes undetected

threat: Consent/token/runtime-control/correlation state persists unexpectedly across localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies, or Cache Storage
attackSurface: Full browser storage surface, real Chromium + Firefox, real vendor SDK
expectedBehavior: Own package code never touches storage APIs; the vendor SDK's own session cookie is the only persisted item and never contains the raw client token; no growth across init->grant->record->revoke->shutdown
testType: live adversarial (Chromium + Firefox, real browser-app page)
residualRisk: LOW — the vendor SDK's own first-party session cookie (`_oo_s`) is an accepted, documented footprint (session id only, no token/PII), inherent to the pinned @openobserve/browser-core 0.3.4 default session-persistence strategy; not owned by this project's own code.

threat: getObservabilityStatus() exposes token, raw config, URL, payload, stack, session ID, credential, or SDK private state
expectedBehavior: Status snapshot only ever contains the documented, bounded top-level fields; never contains forbidden substrings even after adversarial recordAction/recordError calls

threat: Any HTTP method/path/encoding/header combination other than the exact two ingestion routes reaches OpenObserve
expectedBehavior: Only POST /rum/v1/default/rum and POST /rum/v1/default/logs proxy upstream; every other org/version/path-traversal/encoding/method/Origin/Host/smuggling variant is denied before proxy_pass
testType: adversarial live proxy matrix (already covered by proxy-security, re-run as regression)

threat: Non-ingestion OpenObserve-shaped paths (management/search/config, replay) fall through to a permissive default instead of an explicit deny
expectedBehavior: Every OpenObserve-shaped path not in the exact ingestion allowlist returns 403/404 with no proxy_pass to openobserve
testType: live adversarial sweep + real admin-side read-back

threat: Holder of the leaked (browser-visible, non-secret-by-design) RUM client token uses it against OpenObserve's admin API (search, stream/schema/settings/delete, dashboard/alert/pipeline/user/org/token management)
attackSurface: OpenObserve admin API, http://127.0.0.1:5080 (loopback-only), independent of the reverse proxy
expectedBehavior: The RUM token is rejected (401) for every admin capability under every plausible auth-header encoding; no state changes as a result of probing
testType: live adversarial capability sweep with read-back

threat: OpenObserve's management port is reachable from outside the host
expectedBehavior: Management UI/API bound to loopback only, never a wildcard/public interface
testType: static compose safety check (reference-lab, re-run as regression) + Docker container inspection

threat: Sensitive content (auth/cookie/JWT/API key/private key/email/PII, prototype keys, unicode homoglyphs, encoded line breaks, oversized values) reaches storage via either the real browser SDK path or a direct proxy path that bypasses the browser sanitizer
expectedBehavior: SAFE -> stored, REDACTED -> safe placeholder, SECRET -> never stored, for both the real SDK path and a direct-to-proxy bypass path
testType: live adversarial dual-path corpus (already covered by sanitization, re-run as regression)

threat: Sensitive content leaks into stream schema, dashboard/alert exports or backups, proxy/access logs, operator status, pipeline diagnostics, or test artifacts
attackSurface: Cross-cutting: every operator-facing surface listed above
expectedBehavior: None of these surfaces ever contain unredacted sensitive content
evidence: scripts/lab/verify-sanitization-leakage.mjs; tests/lab/dashboards/audit.test.js; tests/lab/alerts/audit.test.js; scripts/lab/dashboards-export.mjs / alerts-export.mjs output format

threat: A schema-valid, correctly multipart-encoded malicious replay request reaches OpenObserve before any server-side content validation
expectedBehavior: Proxy returns 404 (no /replay location exists) before any proxy_pass; no data lands in _sessionreplay
residualRisk: NONE — Session Replay remains permanently closed by design; see docs/session-replay-security-decision.md.

threat: Session Replay is silently re-enabled somewhere in config, runtime code, or the operator plane
attackSurface: runtime config schema, browser adapter, proxy config, dashboards/alerts
expectedBehavior: Config schema cannot express replay enablement; sample rate is always 0; no startSessionReplayRecording call exists; no dashboard/alert references it

threat: Adversarial control documents (malformed JSON, duplicate/unknown keys, negative/rollback revision, future issuedAt, expired/TTL-overflow, wrong enum) open collection instead of failing closed
expectedBehavior: Every adversarial document is rejected by the browser package's own validation (fail closed), regardless of what the served bytes actually contain
testType: live adversarial (write raw bytes directly to the served location, bypassing the operator's own pre-write validator)

threat: Symlink replacement of the runtime-writable proxy-gate file lets an attacker write through to an arbitrary host path
expectedBehavior: Write is refused when the target path is a symlink; the symlink target is never modified

threat: Concurrent/simultaneous kill-switch on and off operations interleave their non-atomic steps, leaving the proxy gate and the control document disagreeing about whether the kill switch is active
expectedBehavior: The two independent kill-switch layers (proxy gate, control document) always agree on final state after a race; no silent inconsistency
evidence: tests/security/adversarial/lab-adversarial.mjs:checkKillSwitchConcurrentRace; fix: scripts/lab/common.mjs withExclusiveLock(), wired into kill-switch.mjs

threat: An active kill switch does not actually stop new RUM ingestion from reaching upstream storage
attackSurface: Reverse proxy $chicek_kill_switch_active gate on both ingestion locations
expectedBehavior: 410 Gone on both ingestion paths; canary content never reaches OpenObserve storage

threat: Pending native SDK queue is assumed purgeable on revoke/shutdown
expectedBehavior: No code or documentation ever claims the native SDK's own retry queue is purged on revoke/shutdown
residualRisk: LOW — accepted, documented residual risk; see docs/telemetry-delivery-security-decision.md.

threat: Destructive operations (delete/settings weakening) reach the canonical _rumdata/_rumlog streams, or a non-disposable-prefixed stream is treated as safe to delete
expectedBehavior: Canonical streams are unconditionally hard-blocked; only exact disposable-prefix + correct org + explicit confirmed:true is ever admitted
testType: adversarial obfuscation-resistance unit test (case variation, whitespace, Cyrillic homoglyph, prototype-shaped names, type-coercion on confirmed, org-scope bypass)

threat: The read-only dashboard/alert auditors crash on malformed/hostile imported JSON instead of flagging it, letting a malformed definition slip past review unaudited
expectedBehavior: Never throws; malformed/unauditable shapes are themselves flagged as a SECURITY_RISK finding rather than crashing the audit
testType: adversarial robustness fuzzing (hostile shapes: non-object root, circular refs, wrong-typed fields, __proto__ keys, deep nesting, oversized SQL)

threat: Dashboard/alert authored queries contain SELECT *, unbounded range, missing service/environment filter, high-cardinality GROUP BY, sensitive fields, custom-JS panels, replay references, or delivery-guarantee claims
expectedBehavior: Every listed category is flagged with the correct risk class

threat: Import/restore/overwrite/delete of dashboards or alerts proceeds without explicit confirmation, or overwrites a company-owned asset
expectedBehavior: SKIP/OVERWRITE only under an explicit conflict policy; company-owned assets are never silently overwritten
testType: unit (already covered by dashboard-governance/17, re-run as regression)

threat: A committed secret (token/password/JWT/private key/webhook/admin credential) exists anywhere under apps/packages/scripts/infrastructure/tests/docs/root
attackSurface: scripts/security/scan-secrets.js scanTrackedFiles() over the real repository
expectedBehavior: Zero findings across every git-tracked file; placeholders/examples/shell-substitution/canaries never false-positive
testType: static scan, real repository + disposable fixture repo
evidence: tests/security/scan-secrets.test.js (unchanged by security-acceptance; re-run as part of pnpm verify)

threat: Dependency versions are not exact-pinned, or an unexpected dependency enters the lockfile/SBOM
expectedBehavior: Frozen lockfile install succeeds with no diff; exact Node/pnpm/dependency versions match .node-version/package.json

threat: A container other than reverse-proxy/openobserve is reachable on a port it should not be able to reach (unexpected admin-endpoint reachability)
attackSurface: Docker network topology: app-internal (reverse-proxy, browser-app, http-test-service) vs observability-internal/edge-publish (openobserve, alert-sink)
expectedBehavior: browser-app and http-test-service cannot reach OpenObserve's admin API at all (different Docker network, not just an app-level auth rejection)

threat: alert-sink (network_mode: service:openobserve, deliberately shares OpenObserve's netns to reach its own loopback-only destination) has access to OpenObserve's admin credentials
expectedBehavior: No admin credential files present in the alert-sink container despite the shared network namespace

threat: Restarting the openobserve container silently breaks alert-sink's shared-network-namespace binding, leaving alert delivery unavailable with healthchecks staying green
expectedBehavior: Operators are aware this restart-order dependency exists; not a data-loss or security-boundary issue (core ingestion is unaffected)
testType: live observation during lab operation (discovered via lab:verify's own restart phases)
result: DOCUMENTED, NOT FIXED (operational note, not a security/privacy defect)
residualRisk: LOW — availability-only, no data exposure; requires restarting alert-sink after any openobserve restart. Recorded as an operational note; fixing would mean restructuring the deliberately loopback-only network design from an earlier stage, out of security-acceptance's minimal-fix scope.

threat: Containers run as root, with a writable root filesystem, retained Linux capabilities, or without no-new-privileges
attackSurface: infrastructure/docker/compose.yaml security posture (user, read_only, cap_drop, security_opt) for every service
expectedBehavior: non-root, read-only fs, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges across all lab containers
testType: static + live container inspection (reference-lab, re-run as regression)
evidence: scripts/lab/verify-containers.mjs (pnpm lab:verify container security posture phase)

threat: TLS certificate SAN/hostname mismatch, or private key world/group readable
expectedBehavior: SAN matches localhost/127.0.0.1; private key file mode 0600
testType: static + live check (reference-lab, re-run as regression)

threat: Alert notification bodies contain raw event/stack data, session lists, URL query/body content, tokens/cookies/identity, destination credentials, or runtime-control document content
attackSurface: OpenObserve destination-test delivery -> mock alert-sink (tests/fixtures/apps/http-test-service sanitizeAlertSinkBody allowlist)
expectedBehavior: None of the forbidden content categories ever reach the captured notification body, even when the destination-test payload is adversarially crafted to include all of them
residualRisk: LOW — this exercises the local test-sink's own allowlist end-to-end via the real destination-test API, not a full real-alert-fires-from-live-data path (which would require waiting out real alert evaluation timing); the static definition-level check (S18-21 / auditAlertDefinition SENSITIVE_OUTPUT) is the primary control for template/row_template content.

threat: Destination failure (sink disabled) causes a retry storm or secret logging, or breaks core frontend/OpenObserve function
attackSurface: OpenObserve destination retry behavior, tests/fixtures/apps/http-test-service alert-sink disable/enable
expectedBehavior: Bounded retry, no secret in logs, core ingestion/query unaffected while the destination is down
testType: live check (already covered by alert-governance, re-run as regression)
